text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A former secretary to the cabinet, Philip Mbithi, prematurely ordered the arrest of the Kenya Ports Authority boss and 19 others last year before investigations were complete, a Mombasa court heard.
- Twelve employees of Standard Chartered Bank Kenya Ltd are arrested in connection with the 96 million shillings ($1.78 million) robbery on Tuesday.
- The suspended chairman of the ruling party Kenya African National Union branch in Uasin Gishu Jackson Kibor is disqualified from on-going party elections for "importing" voters.
- Giant dairy milk body Kenya Cooperative Creameries will convert to a limited liability company if the proposal is approved at an Annual General Meeting in April.
- Hundred of hectares of grassland and indigenous trees have been destroyed by a fire that has swept through Mount Kenya forest over the last three days.
- Pressure mounts for embattled Public Accounts Chairman Michael Kijana Wamalwa to resign or risk the wrath of the House.
